??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Good evening, *Player*. Forgive me if I correct you later; I correct everyone who gets a chieftain's name wrong, even Old Ones. Especially Old Ones.
    - Odda gave me two verses I had half forgotten, and Thrun gave me one I had never heard, which he insists his grandmother sang while churning butter. The song is a little longer tonight than it was.
    - Imre's dates: the shimmering nights, and after each one the worst stirring of the season. I have kept songs for thirty-five years and I cannot tell you what it means. I can only tell you it is so.
    - The hounds, the masks, the wild goats, the gnawers. I have decided: the verse is true, as far as a verse can be. Whether it is sung is not mine alone to decide.
    - I sang it at the gathering, before all four families: a season when the beasts grew wild, before the Burning. The song does not say what it means. It is sung again, and the families heard it together.
    - What would you hear?
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* What troubles you?
        - *Choice:* Who is the stargazer?
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Ahvi, song-keeper of the Brenna. Old Hadda taught me from the age of eight. I sang the long song at my sister Varra's choosing, and through the whole night of Hask's choosing, and at dawn I added his name after hers.
    - There is a short verse in the oldest part of the long songs, among the chieftains of the Age of Division: goats that bite, cats that hunt people, birds that will not settle, a season before the Burning. I have sung it alone every night this summer.
    - It is sung now, and it will be in Neffa's lessons. She will learn it properly. Not yet. But properly.
    - Imre and I swap star stories on the high terrace on clear nights: lowland names for Brenna stars, Brenna songs for lowland stars. Imre forgets supper and never forgets a star. I suspect a song is being written up there, though nobody has told me so.
    - Good night. Mind the names.
